title: Horizontal and composite-adjunction pasting of enhanced mates
statement:
Use enriched infinity categories and enhanced functor categories as in [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal]. An enhanced adjunction means an equivalence of enriched mapping bifunctors, with enhanced unit and counit and coherent triangle identities. All functors, transformations, parameter diagrams and homotopies below are enhanced data, rather than data supplied only on ordinary homotopy categories. Use the unit-and-counit mate word of [lem-coef-dg-mate-transpose], whose ordinary directions are those of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Composition is read right to left.

(1) Let $L_i:\mathcal C_i\rightleftarrows\mathcal D_i:R_i$ ($i=1,2,3$) be enhanced adjunctions with units $\eta_i$ and counits $\epsilon_i$. Let $G:\mathcal C_1\to\mathcal C_2$, $H:\mathcal D_1\to\mathcal D_2$, $G':\mathcal C_2\to\mathcal C_3$ and $H':\mathcal D_2\to\mathcal D_3$ be enhanced functors, and let $\alpha:L_2G\to HL_1$ and $\alpha':L_3G'\to H'L_2$ have mates $\beta:GR_1\to R_2H$ and $\beta':G'R_2\to R_3H'$. The mate of the horizontally pasted transformation
$$(H'\alpha)(\alpha'G):L_3G'G\longrightarrow H'HL_1$$
is coherently identified with
$$(\beta'H)(G'\beta):G'GR_1\longrightarrow R_3H'H.$$

(2) Let $L_i:\mathcal C_i\rightleftarrows\mathcal D_i:R_i$ and $L_i':\mathcal D_i\rightleftarrows\mathcal E_i:R_i'$ ($i=1,2$) be enhanced adjunctions with units $\eta_i,\eta_i'$ and counits $\epsilon_i,\epsilon_i'$. Let $G:\mathcal C_1\to\mathcal C_2$, $H:\mathcal D_1\to\mathcal D_2$ and $K:\mathcal E_1\to\mathcal E_2$ be enhanced functors. Given $\alpha:L_2G\to HL_1$ and $\gamma:L_2'H\to KL_1'$ with mates $\beta:GR_1\to R_2H$ and $\delta:HR_1'\to R_2'K$, the mate under the composite adjunctions $L_i'L_i\dashv R_iR_i'$ of
$$(\gamma L_1)(L_2'\alpha):L_2'L_2G\longrightarrow KL_1'L_1$$
is coherently identified with
$$(R_2\delta)(\beta R_1'):GR_1R_1'\longrightarrow R_2R_2'K.$$
The composite adjunction units and counits used here are $(R_i\eta_i'L_i)\eta_i$ and $\epsilon_i'(L_i'\epsilon_iR_i')$, respectively.

Both comparisons are natural on the full enhanced transformation objects. For any specified coherent parameter diagram of these data, they hold as homotopies on all its simplices, compatible with faces, degeneracies, identities and iterated pasting.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, specified adjunction mates: horizontal and composite-adjunction pasting identities and coherent parameter homotopies. This is an agent-formulated foundation; no Stacks tag states the enhanced assertion.

proof.text:
Work throughout in enhanced functor categories, with coherent reassociations understood. By [lem-coef-dg-mate-transpose], transposition is an equivalence of full transformation objects. Write it as $T_L(t)=\epsilon B\circ Lt$ for $t:A\to RB$; its inverse is $s\mapsto Rs\circ\eta A$. This general form follows by taking the first adjunction to be the identity in that node. Its inverse homotopies are the supplied coherent triangles. For the specified mates this gives
$$\epsilon_2H\circ L_2\beta\simeq H\epsilon_1\circ\alpha R_1,$$
and the corresponding equation for every other square. Composition and whiskering take place on the enhanced functor categories of [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal]. Thus all calculations below are homotopies there. Comparing transposes transports a path back by an equivalence of transformation objects; it is not an inference from equality on $H^0$.

source.place: Agent proof, step 1: enhanced transposition equivalence and its unit/counit formulas. The cited blueprint is application context only; this calculation is supplied here and is not in that source.

proof.text:
In (1) put $q=(\beta'H)(G'\beta)$. Its $L_3$-transpose has the following path, where the first and third lines use the transpose equation of [lem-coef-dg-mate-transpose], and the middle line is enhanced naturality of $\alpha'$ at the transformation $\beta$:
$$\begin{aligned}
\epsilon_3H'H\circ L_3q
&\simeq H'\epsilon_2H\circ\alpha'R_2H\circ L_3G'\beta\\
&\simeq H'\epsilon_2H\circ H'L_2\beta\circ\alpha'GR_1\\
&\simeq H'H\epsilon_1\circ H'\alpha R_1\circ\alpha'GR_1.
\end{aligned}$$
The last expression is $H'H\epsilon_1\circ((H'\alpha)(\alpha'G))R_1$, precisely the transpose of the mate of the pasted square. Apply the inverse enhanced transpose equivalence to this displayed path. This constructs the comparison in (1) without a claim that an ordinary mate identity lifts automatically.

source.place: Agent proof, step 2: horizontal mate-pasting comparison by the displayed transpose calculation. The cited blueprint is application context only; this calculation is supplied here and is not in that source.

proof.text:
For (2), compose the given equivalences of enriched mapping bifunctors:
$$\mathcal E_i(L_i'L_iX,Z)\simeq\mathcal D_i(L_iX,R_i'Z)\simeq\mathcal C_i(X,R_iR_i'Z).$$
The forward word sends $h$ to $R_iR_i'(h)\,R_i\eta_i'L_i\,\eta_i$, so evaluating at the identity gives the unit $(R_i\eta_i'L_i)\eta_i$. The inverse word sends $g$ to $\epsilon_i'\,L_i'\epsilon_iR_i'\,L_i'L_ig$, so its identity evaluation gives the counit $\epsilon_i'(L_i'\epsilon_iR_i')$. Composing the inverse-equivalence homotopies supplies the coherent triangles, since these are composites of the given enriched mapping equivalences, rather than newly chosen homotopies. The same words apply to transformations in functor categories by [lem-coef-dg-mate-transpose]. In particular the transpose under this composite adjunction is successive transposition, first under $L_2$, then under $L_2'$.

source.place: Agent proof, step 3: composite mapping equivalences and the composite unit/counit formulas. The cited blueprint is application context only; this calculation is supplied here and is not in that source.

proof.text:
Put $q=(R_2\delta)(\beta R_1')$. Its first transpose is
$$\epsilon_2R_2'K\circ L_2q\simeq\delta\circ\epsilon_2HR_1'\circ L_2\beta R_1'\simeq\delta\circ H\epsilon_1R_1'\circ\alpha R_1R_1'.$$
Here the first path is counit naturality at $\delta$, and the second is the transpose equation for $\beta$ from [lem-coef-dg-mate-transpose]. Its further transpose under $L_2'$ is
$$\begin{aligned}
&\epsilon_2'K\circ L_2'\delta\circ L_2'H\epsilon_1R_1'\circ L_2'\alpha R_1R_1'\\
&\quad\simeq K\epsilon_1'\circ\gamma R_1'\circ L_2'H\epsilon_1R_1'\circ L_2'\alpha R_1R_1'\\
&\quad\simeq K\epsilon_1'\circ KL_1'\epsilon_1R_1'\circ\gamma L_1R_1R_1'\circ L_2'\alpha R_1R_1'.
\end{aligned}$$
The paths are respectively the transpose equation for $\delta$ and naturality of $\gamma$ at $\epsilon_1R_1'$. The last word is the composite counit from step 3 followed by the pasted square evaluated on $R_1R_1'$. It is therefore the composite-adjunction transpose of its mate. Inverting the successive transpose equivalences gives (2).

source.place: Agent proof, step 4: composite-adjunction mate-pasting comparison by successive transposes. The cited blueprint is application context only; this calculation is supplied here and is not in that source.

proof.text: Perform the displayed calculations on the full transformation objects: the inputs $\alpha,\alpha',\gamma$ vary there, their mate words are composites of enhanced functors, and every path used above is a whiskered naturality homotopy or an inverse-equivalence homotopy of transposition. The parameter-restriction clause of [lem-coef-dg-mate-transpose] and the coherent-diagram/substitution clause of [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal] apply to these operations themselves. For a specified parameter diagram pull back this entire construction, including the paths and inverse-equivalence homotopies, along each simplex. Pullback along a face or degeneracy is the same construction on that face or degeneracy, giving the asserted compatible homotopies. Identity insertions use the coherent unit maps for composition. For iterated pasting use successive transposition of the full string: its forward and inverse words are the successive adjunction equivalences of step 3; reassociating them is the coherent associativity of composition in the enhanced functor categories. The binary comparisons above were obtained by that same transposition and naturality, so substitution into the string gives their higher compatibility diagrams. Thus no arbitrary filling of a diagram, nor equality detected only on ordinary homotopy categories, is used.
